raw_response:
I've been working this same land for 50 years. I know every patch of it. At 65, living alone, I can't overwork myself, so I stick to what I know gives me a reliable harvest.

The wheat goes in first, in October, on all 4.1 mu — that's the foundation of my year. I'll rotary till after maize harvest in late September to loosen the soil and chop the stubble. I buy improved wheat seed from the county supply station, the same variety I've used the past few years, gives decent yield and doesn't lodge easily. For fertilizer I mix in compound fertilizer (nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium) as base and put down urea at jointing in March. I irrigate three times — before freeze-up in November, at green-up in February, and at heading in April. I spray herbicide in November and a fungicide pass in April when powdery mildew risk goes up. I expect around 450 jin per mu, which is what I usually get.

Come June, right after wheat harvest, I turn around and plant summer maize on the same 4.1 mu. I don't plow — no time and my back won't take it. I use a hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the station recommends that's similar. I apply compound fertilizer as base and top-dress with urea at the big bell stage. Summer rains help a lot, I only pump from the well once or twice if August is dry. I spray once for corn borer and once if I see blight. Harvest in late September. I expect maybe 520 to 550 jin per mu.
